topic.title: the Microsoft outage
topic.claim: When Outlook and Teams went down, your work didn't stop. Only the proof that you were working did.
topic.moment: Friday morning, Teams won't load, Outlook spins, and after the first panic your day goes strangely quiet and you get the one real task done by lunch.

turn.actually: It stops the signals of work: the green dot, the instant reply, the cc to your boss. A lot of your day is spent making those signals.

topic.because: Your boss can't see your work, only your replies. So you stay green, reply in seconds and cc people, because that is what looks like work. Take the tools away and the signal goes, and the real work turns out to be smaller and quieter than the day felt.
topic.payoff: The outage took away the stage, not the work. Notice how your day felt without an audience.
topic.villain: an office that judges you by how fast you reply, not by what you finish
topic.behaviour: office workers spend much of the day replying, staying online and cc-ing to look busy
topic.mechanism: when work is invisible, people manage what is visible: replies and online status, so a tool outage removes the performance and leaves the actual work
topic.group: salaried office workers in India on Microsoft Teams and Outlook
topic.send_to: the colleague who spent today refreshing Teams to see if it's back
topic.why_now: Microsoft 365's global outage from late Thursday 12 Nov into Friday 13 Nov 2026 took down Outlook, Teams and Copilot
topic.news_peg: Microsoft 365 global outage, 12-13 November 2026: Outlook, Teams and Copilot down for over 12 hours

sources.fact: A Microsoft 365 outage that began Thursday 12 November 2026 at 1:26 PM ET (11:56 PM IST) disrupted Outlook, Teams, Copilot, OneDrive and other Microsoft services worldwide.
sources.excerpt: outage began Thursday at 1:26 PM ET | Downdetector complaints covered Outlook, Microsoft 365, Teams, Copilot, Azure, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Store | customers may be unable to connect to multiple services | As of 6:57 PM ET the ongoing Microsoft 365 outage has not yet been resolved | limited recovery

sources.fact: On Friday 13 November 2026 the global outage hitting Outlook, Teams and Copilot was still unresolved more than 12 hours in; Microsoft said there was no indication of a cyber attack.
sources.excerpt: Microsoft outage affects users worldwide, impacting Teams, Outlook and Copilot | still ongoing as of 5:06pm AEDT Friday 13 November | partial recovery that was not sustained | no indication this is a cyber attack | reverting a recent network configuration change

_ledger.text:
[cover] India would never let one company own UPI.
But we happily let one American company own the workday.
 

[slide 1] India would never let one company own UPI.
But we happily let one American company own the workday.

[slide 2] Around midnight on Thursday, Outlook, Teams and Copilot went down.
By morning your whole office was waiting on one company to switch it back on.

[slide 3] Your IT team couldn't fix it. Your CEO couldn't escalate it.
All anyone could do was wait for Microsoft's next update.

[slide 4] That isn't a tech glitch. It's a choice we made.
For money, we built shared rails nobody owns alone. For work, we just bought a subscription.

[slide 5] Nobody's asking you to quit Teams.
But a country that refused to hand its payments to one company shouldn't hand it the office.

[slide 6] Today the entire office had one boss.
And he was on leave.

[end card] 
Send this to the friend in IT who spent the morning refreshing Microsoft's status page.

[caption] The Microsoft outage showed that Indian offices run on one switch, and one company holds it.

We kept UPI on shared rails so no single company could stop our money. Our workday never got that rule.

Send this to the friend in IT who spent the morning refreshing Microsoft's status page.

2d7188d7fef8ecafc8be2238dd9f19a34f363ac2.actual_mechanism: Outlook, Teams and Copilot are Microsoft 365 services Microsoft runs on its own Azure cloud (physical datacenters), and the Nov 12-13, 2026 incident began with an Exchange Online failure (~16:17 UTC Nov 12) that cascaded across Teams, SharePoint, Copilot and even third-party AI tools using M365 connectors, hitting 74 countries within an hour. The cloud market is genuinely concentrated: AWS, Azure and Google Cloud together hold roughly two-thirds (~67%) of global cloud infrastructure, so unrelated firms and direct competitors do commonly depend on the same few providers, and a single provider's failure takes down everyone renting from it simultaneously, everywhere.

ledger.text: Premise: the everyday work tools offices depend on for email, chat, meetings and documents are, despite feeling like many separate tools, actually built and owned by only a handful of large tech companies. Premise: when Microsoft's Outlook and Teams went down in this outage, offices did not go tool-free or self-reliant; they simply moved their work onto WhatsApp, a product owned by Meta, another large tech company.
